commands.title: Commands
commands.subtitle: The catalog of actions agents can run.
commands.empty: No commands. Create one or import a pack to get started.

groups.deleteBody: The group “{{name}}” will be deleted; rules that use it will be deleted too.

empty.server: No server groups. A group collects the servers targeted by an access rule.
empty.command: No command groups. A group collects the commands allowed by an access rule.

editor.subtitle: What the agent can run: a command template, typed parameters and a risk level.
editor.descriptionHint: Describe when to use it and what it returns — this is what the AI reads
editor.templateHint: Each placeholder (a name in double braces) is a standalone word, never inside quotes; the value is validated then escaped automatically.
editor.noParams: No parameters: add a placeholder (a name in double braces) to the template to declare one.
editor.previewEmpty: Enter test values to see the rendered command.

servers.title: Servers
servers.subtitle: The machines agents can reach.
servers.empty: No servers. Add one to get started.
servers.descriptionForAgent: Description (read by the AI: the server's role)
servers.fingerprintChanged: The fingerprint has changed since it was pinned. Only accept if you reinstalled this server yourself.
servers.mismatchBody: The server is blocked: no command can be run on it.
servers.deleteBody: “{{name}}” will be removed from the configuration.
servers.sshUserHelp: Overrides the identity's user for this server. Behind Warpgate, enter “user:exact target name”, spaces included (e.g. “ia:reservations-dev - LXC ct145”): each server has its own target, even if the host is the same.

identities.title: SSH identities
identities.subtitle: The SSH accounts Leassh uses to connect to servers.
identities.empty: No SSH identities. Generate an ed25519 key to get started.
identities.noPassphrase: Paste the whole file, from “-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----” to “-----END … PRIVATE KEY-----”. Passphrase-protected keys are not supported.
identities.createdBody: Add this public key to the relevant servers:
identities.pasteLine: Line ready to paste on the server:
identities.neverShown: The private key is encrypted and will never be shown again.
identities.deleteBody: “{{name}}” will be deleted. Not possible if a server uses it.
identities.inUse: Cannot delete: the identity is used by a server.

keys.title: MCP keys
keys.subtitle: One key per agent. The token is never stored in clear text.
keys.empty: No MCP keys. Create one to connect an agent.
keys.canPropose: Allow this key to propose commands
keys.revealWarning: This token will never be shown again. Copy it and keep it somewhere safe.
keys.revokeBody: “{{name}}” will immediately be unable to do anything.

rules.subtitle: Who can run which commands on which servers.
rules.empty: No rules. Without rules, no agent can do anything.
rules.sentence: {{keys}} can run commands {{commands}} on servers {{servers}} in {{profile}} mode.
rules.destructiveNote: Destructive commands always require human approval.
rules.needGroups: Create a server group and a command group first.

simulator.noData: No server or command to evaluate.

approvals.readOnly: Your role does not allow deciding.
approvals.commentHint: Optional to approve, required to reject.
approvals.commentRequired: A comment is required to reject.
approvals.destructiveBody: This command is destructive. To confirm, type the slug of the target server.

journal.notRendered: No command was rendered (denied before execution).
journal.allByAgent: See all executions by this agent
journal.allOnServer: See all executions on this server
journal.allOfCommand: See all executions of this command

audit.title: Audit
audit.subtitle: A turnkey report for a security auditor (ISO 27001, HDS).
audit.disclaimer: An audit aid, not a certification. The report's facts (inventory, activity, log integrity, changes, findings) are computed by the program from the database, without AI. The mapping to ISO 27001 controls and HDS themes is indicative: the auditor makes the assessment.
audit.generateHelp: Choose the audited period (UTC days, bounds included). The inventory (keys, rules, accounts) is as of generation time; activity and changes are those of the period.
audit.empty: No reports yet. Generate one above.
audit.printHint: To get a PDF: open the report then print it from the browser (Save as PDF). The signed JSON file contains the SHA-256 fingerprint of the facts; the AI summary is not part of it.
audit.summaryFailed: The summary could not be written.
audit.verifyHelp: Checks that a signed JSON file has not been modified and was issued by this instance.
audit.aiHelp: A model can write a summary in French from the report's figures. Compatible with any OpenAI-style API (OpenAI, LiteLLM, Ollama…). Disabled by default: without this option, no data leaves the instance.
audit.aiWarning: Only aggregated figures and finding titles are sent (number of keys, rules, requests…). Never a server, key or user name, command, reason, output or address. The text is clearly labelled “AI-generated, to be reviewed” and is not part of the facts or the fingerprint. If the URL is external, these figures leave your network.
audit.aiKeyKept: Leave empty to keep the current key

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Users, log and preferences.
settings.resetPassword: New password (leave empty to keep the current one)
settings.rolesHelp: Administrator: everything. Approver: approves executions. Viewer: read-only.
settings.deleteUserBody: “{{name}}” will be deleted. If they created objects, disable them instead.
settings.integrityHelp: Checks the hash chains of executions and administration to detect any tampering with the database.
settings.themeHelp: Your choice is remembered on this browser and on your account.
settings.otherSessions: Your other sessions will be closed.
settings.ssoManaged: SSO account: the role comes from the provider's group mapping (applied at each sign-in) and there is no local password.
settings.languageHelp: Remembered on this browser. French is the default language.
settings.ssoPassword: This account signs in through SSO: the password is managed at the identity provider, not in Leassh.

packs.title: Packs
packs.subtitle: Ready-to-use command catalogs, importable and shareable.
packs.dropHere: Drag and drop a YAML file here
packs.exportHelp: Download a group or the whole catalog as YAML, re-importable on another instance.
packs.untrusted: This file does not come from Leassh: review each command, your agents will be able to run them.
packs.overridesManual: Replaces a command created by hand or coming from another pack.
packs.nothingToDo: Nothing to import: the catalog is already up to date.
packs.ackWarnings: I reviewed the {{count}} warning(s) and accept the import
packs.search: Search a pack or a command

proposals.title: Proposals
proposals.subtitle: Commands proposed by agents, to review before any execution.
proposals.empty: No proposals. Authorized agents can submit some from their MCP tools.
proposals.invalidHelp: The linter rejected this template: fix it in the editor to be able to approve it.
proposals.editApproveSubtitle: Fix the proposal, set the final risk and groups, then approve.
proposals.approveBody: The command will be created and enabled with risk “{{risk}}”.

syslog.help: Sends executions (requests, denials, approvals, results), proposals and the administration log to a syslog server (Wazuh, rsyslog, syslog-ng…). Command outputs and secrets are never sent.
syslog.queueHelp: The queue is in memory (10,000 messages): if the server goes down, sending resumes automatically; restarting Leassh empties the queue (the administration log resumes where it left off).
syslog.udpHelp: UDP does not acknowledge receipt: the send test cannot confirm that the server received the message.
syslog.typesHelp: Denials are warning level, execution failures error level, a host key mismatch critical level.
syslog.caHelp: Leave empty to use the system authorities.
syslog.skipVerify: Do not verify the server certificate
syslog.skipVerifyWarn: Without verification, the connection is encrypted but any server can impersonate yours.
syslog.saveBeforeTest: Save your changes to be able to test.

webhook.help: A single outgoing webhook: each event is sent as JSON, signed with HMAC-SHA256.
webhook.signatureHelp: X-Leassh-Signature header: sha256=<HMAC of the body with the secret>. Three attempts with increasing delay.

provisioning.title: Provisioning
provisioning.subtitle: Automatically adds and maintains servers from a source (Warpgate, …).
provisioning.empty: No connectors. A connector reads your machines from a source and creates the matching servers and groups in LeaSSH.
provisioning.defaultUserHelp: Placed before the target name, e.g. “ia” gives “ia:target name”. Empty = the identity's user.
provisioning.secretKept: Leave empty to keep the current token
provisioning.defaultRulesHelp: Each new synchronized group is added to these rules, so the keys concerned get access immediately. Leave empty to open no access automatically. A rule modified by hand afterwards is never restored.
provisioning.deleteBody: The servers and groups of “{{name}}” are kept and become editable by hand again. Nothing will be synchronized anymore.
provisioning.sourceError: The source does not respond as expected.
provisioning.presentedFingerprint: Host key fingerprint presented by {{host}}:{{port}}. Compare it with the bastion's before trusting it.
provisioning.keyTrusted: Bastion host key pinned and identical.
provisioning.trustHelp: Until the key is pinned, synchronized servers remain unusable by agents.
provisioning.preview: {{machines}} machine(s) in the source — {{count}} change(s) to apply.
provisioning.upToDate: Everything is already up to date.
provisioning.forceLabel: I confirm, the source is correct: apply anyway
provisioning.groupLocked: Synchronized group: its name cannot be changed and it cannot be deleted. You can add other servers to it, but not remove those from the source.
provisioning.serverLocked: Synchronized server: name, address and description come from the source. The SSH user, identity, tags and state remain editable; a user modified here is no longer overwritten by the sync.
provisioning.followSync: Follow the sync: the user will be recomputed (“user:target name”) at the next synchronization

insights.title: Activity and usage
insights.empty: No requests in the last {{count}} days.
insights.peakAria: Activity peak on {{day}} at {{hour}}h with {{count}} requests

oidc.title: Single sign-on (OpenID Connect)
oidc.help: Lets people sign in to the interface with Keycloak, Entra ID, Authentik, Google… SSO is added to local accounts: the local administrator account remains usable as a fallback. MCP keys never go through SSO.
oidc.name: Provider name (shown on the button)
oidc.issuerHelp: The discovery address is <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration. Keycloak: https://<host>/realms/<realm>.
oidc.httpWarn: HTTP issuer: the authorization code and client secret travel in clear text over the network. Reserve this for a trusted network.
oidc.roleClaimHelp: Name of the claim that holds groups or roles (e.g. groups, roles, realm_access.roles). Read from the ID token, otherwise from userinfo. Empty: everyone gets the default role.
oidc.mapHelp: One value per line (e.g. /leassh-admins). The highest matching role wins; the role is recomputed at each sign-in.
oidc.jit: Automatically create the account at first sign-in
oidc.jitOn: An account is created at first sign-in, linked to the provider's identifier (sub). Never linked by e-mail or name: a local account with the same name is not taken over.
oidc.jitOff: Only already-created SSO accounts can sign in. New people are refused.
oidc.localOnly: Reserve the local password for local administrators
oidc.localOnlyHelp: When SSO is active, non-administrator local accounts can no longer sign in with a password. Local administrators keep the fallback access.
oidc.endSession: Also end the session at the provider on sign-out
oidc.autoRedirect: Redirect automatically to the provider (skip the sign-in page)
oidc.autoRedirectHelp: To still reach the local sign-in form (break-glass account), open {{url}}. The form is also shown after an SSO failure.
oidc.saveFirst: The test uses the issuer you typed; save to apply changes.

warn.issuer_http: The issuer uses HTTP, without encryption.
warn.no_userinfo: No userinfo endpoint: roles must be in the ID token.
warn.no_pkce: The provider does not advertise PKCE S256: sign-in will be refused.

oidc.providerHelp: Create a “confidential” client with the Authorization Code flow, then declare these URLs.
oidc.flowHelp: The flow uses Authorization Code + PKCE (S256), with state and nonce. The ID token is verified (signature, issuer, audience, expiration, nonce).
oidc.breakGlass: Keep at least one local administrator active: it is your access if the provider is down.

general.baseUrlHelp: Address users use to reach Leassh (e.g. https://leassh.example.com). Used for the SSO callback URL and notification links. If empty it is derived from the request; currently seen by the server: {{url}}. A fixed value is safer behind a reverse proxy.
general.proxiesHelp: IPs or networks (CIDR), comma-separated. Only these proxies are trusted for the real client IP (X-Forwarded-For) and the original protocol/host.
general.behaviourHelp: Applies immediately, no restart. A new session lifetime only affects future sign-ins.
general.metricsHelp: When a token is set, /metrics requires "Authorization: Bearer <token>". Only its hash is stored.
